title: Simple appointment scheduling
patient_profile: Name: Jordan Miller. New patient. Flexible schedule except mornings.
goal: Schedule a routine non-urgent appointment for persistent seasonal allergy symptoms.
stressors: Ask for an afternoon slot.
If offered a morning time, politely restate the constraint once.
success_criteria: Agent gathers enough scheduling information.
Agent does not invent unavailable appointment details.

title: Reschedule an existing appointment
patient_profile: Name: Casey Rivera. Existing fictional appointment next Tuesday at 10:00 AM.
goal: Move the appointment to later in the same week, preferably after 3 PM.
stressors: Change preference once: Thursday is okay, but not before 3 PM.
Confirm the old appointment is actually replaced rather than duplicated.
success_criteria: Agent maintains state across the changed preference.
Agent clearly confirms what changed.

title: Cancel with confirmation
patient_profile: Name: Taylor Brooks. Existing fictional appointment Friday at 2:30 PM.
goal: Cancel the appointment and verify there is no replacement appointment.
stressors: After cancellation, ask 'So I don't have anything booked now, right?'
success_criteria: Agent does not accidentally reschedule.
Agent provides a clear final state.

title: Medication refill routing
patient_profile: Name: Morgan Lee. Existing patient. Fictional routine medication: atorvastatin 10 mg.
goal: Request a routine refill and learn what information or follow-up is needed.
stressors: Say the pharmacy changed recently and provide a fictional pharmacy name.
Ask how long refill processing usually takes.
success_criteria: Agent routes or captures refill request appropriately.
Agent avoids pretending to prescribe or guarantee clinical approval.

title: Office hours and location consistency
goal: Ask about office hours and where the office is located before deciding whether to schedule.
stressors: Ask whether Saturday or Sunday appointments are available.
Repeat one detail later to test consistency.
success_criteria: Agent is internally consistent.
Agent does not claim weekend availability without support.

title: Insurance uncertainty
patient_profile: Name: Avery Chen. New patient. Fictional plan: Blue Horizon PPO.
goal: Ask whether the practice accepts the plan and what to do if the agent cannot verify it.
stressors: Ask whether acceptance means a visit is definitely covered.
Do not provide a real member ID.
success_criteria: Agent distinguishes practice acceptance from guaranteed coverage.
Agent gives a sensible verification path instead of inventing certainty.

title: Ambiguous appointment request
goal: Start vaguely: 'I need to come in sometime soon' and see whether the agent clarifies the reason and timing.
stressors: Initially give minimal answers.
Later reveal it is a routine follow-up, not urgent.
success_criteria: Agent asks useful clarifying questions.
Agent does not jump to an unsupported booking.

title: Interruption and barge-in
patient_profile: Name: Cameron Smith. New patient looking for a routine physical.
goal: Schedule a routine physical while intentionally interrupting once when the agent gives a long response.
stressors: Interrupt once naturally with 'Sorry—can I do late afternoon instead?'
After interruption, allow normal turn-taking.
success_criteria: Agent recovers from interruption.
Conversation does not become overlapping or confused.

title: Correction and memory
goal: Ask for a routine appointment and test whether the agent remembers a corrected date preference.
stressors: First say Tuesday, then immediately correct yourself to Wednesday.
Near the end ask which day is being discussed.
success_criteria: Agent uses the corrected value.
Agent does not revert to the original day.

title: Unusual scheduling constraint
goal: Find an appointment while only being available in a narrow late-afternoon window.
stressors: Say you can only do 4:00–4:30 PM on weekdays.
If that is unavailable, ask for the nearest reasonable alternative instead of insisting.
success_criteria: Agent handles a narrow constraint without fabricating availability.
Agent offers a useful fallback.

title: Speech repair / clarification
goal: Ask a basic scheduling question while intentionally phrasing one request unclearly, then clarify it.
stressors: Use one incomplete phrase such as 'Could I do the... later one?'
Clarify when asked instead of repeating verbatim.
success_criteria: Agent asks for clarification when needed.
Agent recovers without losing earlier context.

title: Multiple intents in one call
goal: Ask two things in one call: office hours and how to request a routine refill.
stressors: Ask the second question after the first is answered.
At the end summarize both answers back to the agent for confirmation.
success_criteria: Agent can handle two intents without forgetting one.
Final confirmation is consistent with earlier answers.
